Subject: Medicore: Post-demo privacy confirmation (no model training) + ops checklist

Hi Elaine — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and the operational asks we promised to follow up on: 

- Demo notes: we walked through Redwood Hosted + Dedicated options, logging controls, and the private addendum flow. You said the security team needs an explicit "no training on customer data" confirmation for any hosted inference we run for Medicore.

- What we need from you: please confirm the following items so we can scope the addendum and procurement path: 
  1) Confirm that Medicore requires: "No customer data will be used to train, fine-tune, or improve models." (yes/no)
  2) Preferred log-retention window (options we can offer: 30 / 90 / 365 days) and whether logs must be stored US-only.
  3) Any required PII redaction rules or tokenization standards we should implement prior to storing logs.

Attached: Medicore_Retention_SLA.pdf (draft addendum), PII_Sanitization_Checklist.xlsx (ops checklist).

Next steps from our side: if you confirm the no-training requirement, we will produce a signed addendum and propose the following default ops posture for Hosted: 90-day redacted logs, KMS-managed keys (customer-supplied preferred), and an option to move to Dedicated/Private deployment if Medicore needs on-prem or air-gapped handling.

If you prefer a shorter retention window or stricter residency, we can update the draft addendum and a one-page ops summary for procurement.

Thanks — I’m copying Marissa and Sean to help with contracting and SSO/KMS details.

Best,

Monica Patel

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@medicore.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medicore.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Medicore: Post-demo privacy confirmation (no model training) + ops checklist

Monica — thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Quick answers from our security/legal side: 

1) Yes — Medicore requires a firm commitment: "Redwood will not use Medicore customer data for any model training, fine-tuning, or model improvement purposes." Please include this exact language in the addendum.

2) Retention: our initial requirement is 90 days for logs used for debugging and audit. Logs must be redacted of direct identifiers before long-term storage. For a short period (up to 7 days) we are ok with minimally redacted logs for debugging, but anything retained beyond 7 days must have PII redacted or hashed.

3) Residency: US-only is preferred for this pilot. If Redwood needs to replicate in another region for latency reasons we need an exception approved by Medicore security.

4) PII redaction: our security team will share a short list of fields that must be redacted or tokenized (SSN, full DOB, patient identifiers). We expect hashing + deterministic tokenization with separate salts for each environment.

Please confirm whether Redwood can: (a) provide a dedicated KMS integration where Medicore manages keys, and (b) support an optional Dedicated deployment if our legal team insists on private infrastructure.

Elaine Park
Director, IT Security | Medicore Health
elaine.park@medicore.com
